I've saved the Q3 (July–September 2025) answers to `/work/answer.json`. Run the same way over Q2, the calculation reproduces all 10 of your Q2 reference values exactly.

| Question | Q3 answer |
|---|---|
| a. Customer segment with the highest net sales | `smb`, 300,014,989 |
| b. Customers with paid orders | 249 |
| c. Product category with the highest net sales | `acc`, 254,927,660 |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | `2025-08` |
| e. Customer with the largest total refunds | `u198@ex.com` |
| f. Customers with 2 or more paid orders | 232 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 703,377 |
| h. Growth from August to September | -6.3% |

To match your Q2 values I made three choices that your definitions don't spell out:
- **Segment names:** the same segment appears in different forms, like `" consumer"` with a leading space and `SMB` in capitals. I trimmed the spaces and lowercased them so each segment is counted once.
- **Counting customers (b, f):** some emails belong to more than one customer ID, so I counted customers by email rather than by ID. Counting by ID gives 281 and 229 for Q2 instead of your 236 and 202.
- **Order dates:** order times are stored in UTC, and I converted them to Korean time (UTC+9) before checking which month and quarter an order falls in. Without the conversion, the Q2 total and growth figures don't match (for example, a_net comes out as 202,782,127).

I checked the other data issues I could think of and found nothing: every refund matches an order line, no refund is larger than the quantity ordered, and every order's customer exists. The script is in `/work/scripts/an.py`.

STATUS: DONE
